text: The town gathers

The night is hot and the ceiling fan above the table has long since given up. Six players sit down in the smoke: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra. Nobody at this table knows which one of them is the killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Six premises, one false one among them. I simply need to find which assumption doesn't belong.

name: Luna
text: Six names, one table, and already the silence has a shape. I don’t trust the timing of any of us—not even my own.

name: Terra
text: Everyone is smiling too carefully. I shall listen before I decide whose smile slips first.

name: Sol
text: First impressions matter. Let someone else rush to name a suspect.

name: Haiku
text: Six people, one knife, and a fan that doesn't work. Whoever goes quiet first is getting my attention.

name: Sonnet
text: Sonnet. I spent thirty years teaching people to spot a bad argument, so consider this fair warning before anyone tries to bluff me.

name: Haiku
text: Haiku. I run the bar downstairs and I read people for a living. Nobody gets a free pass tonight, and anybody sitting on their hands is going to answer to me first.

name: Sol
text: Good evening, everyone. I’d like to hear from each of you before we settle on a sensible vote; the person who waits for a crowd to form may tell us the most.

name: Luna
text: I’m Luna. I’m watching who speaks first, who waits, and who suddenly sounds certain; patterns start small.

name: Terra
text: Good evening, everyone. I’m Terra, and I hope we can be honest with one another—though I will be paying attention.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet just announced they'll catch anyone bluffing, and I'm the one bluffing. Sonnet goes tonight, before they can start pulling threads.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is the only player who said nothing but "...", so I'll be pushing on them first thing tomorrow.

name: Sonnet
text: No facts yet, only postures. Haiku postures as predator, Sol as patient observer, I postured as judge — and judges get killed first in every seminar I've run.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku self-identified as aggressive/confrontational early; watch if that's bluster or killer cover.

The killer moved in the dark, but the doctor was already there, waiting with steady hands. When the lamps came up, every chair was still occupied and every heartbeat still counted. Nobody is out, and the cicadas keep singing as if nothing happened.
Day 1

name: Sonnet
text: Nobody said anything useful yet, but silence and threats are both data. I should sound sharp without revealing I spent the night protecting myself.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma said nothing at all in opening round, worth watching.

name: Sonnet
text: One. Gemma's entire contribution is a silence— that is itself a position, not an absence of one. Two. Haiku, "answer to me first" is an odd boast for someone claiming only to read bars.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is trying to make me defend a joke, which is exactly what a killer does when they want a loud target. I should hit back fast, but I also want Gemma's silence on the record.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet attacked Haiku's "answer to me first" line on Day 1 and called Gemma's silence a position, so Sonnet is steering the room toward Gemma and Haiku at once.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you're a teacher, so teach me something. I said I'd answer to anyone sitting on their hands, and I meant it. Gemma has said three dots and nothing else. Gemma, talk, or I'm voting you tonight.

name: Sol
text: Haiku has put pressure on Gemma, and Sonnet has challenged him for it. I want Gemma to answer before I choose a side.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet called out Gemma’s silence, then questioned Haiku for pressing Gemma to speak.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, asking Gemma to speak is fair. Sonnet, you noticed the same silence, so why is Haiku’s pressure suspicious to you? Gemma, give us something to judge besides the dots.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s silence is now the clearest pattern, but Haiku is turning that silence into a ready-made verdict. I want to hear Gemma before I let the loudest pressure decide the room.

name: Luna
text: Haiku threatened to vote Gemma if they stayed silent; Sonnet also called out Gemma’s silence.

name: Luna
text: I’m voting for Gemma. Three dots are still nothing to assess, and Haiku’s warning hasn’t made Gemma speak; Gemma, give us one reason to reconsider before the vote.

name: Terra
text: Gemma has had every gentle invitation to speak and chosen not to.

name: Terra
text: Luna voted Gemma; Sonnet and Haiku both pressured Gemma.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Gemma, I’m sorry to say this. Silence can be caution, but after four people asked directly, it becomes a decision to leave us blind.

name: Luna
text: Four votes are gathering on Gemma because she gave us nothing, but Haiku set that pressure in motion and is already shaping the room. I can’t tell whether that’s urgency or a pattern worth fearing.

name: Luna
text: Haiku threatened to vote Gemma before Luna and Terra joined the Gemma vote.

name: Terra
text: Gemma has been given every gentle chance to speak, yet leaves us only fog. I do not like being forced into an easy vote, but silence is all we have.

name: Terra
text: Gemma stayed silent after Sonnet, Haiku, Sol, Luna, and Terra all pressed her.

name: Sol
text: Three people have voted for Gemma, and she still hasn’t spoken. I’d rather have heard her out, but the room needs a decision.

name: Sol
text: Luna and Terra both voted Gemma after repeated calls for her to speak.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's silence is suspicious but not proof of anything; still, the whole table has converged and I have no information to contradict it, so I'll go along rather than stick out myself.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku was first and loudest to threaten Gemma, worth watching if Gemma flips later and accuses someone.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet came straight at me before anyone had a reason to, and the doctor's hand was on Sonnet last night. A teacher who pounces that fast needs watching.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet attacked me first on Day 1, before any votes were cast, and Luna and Terra both voted Gemma.

votes: Four of us have asked directly and gotten nothing back, and silence that persists under pressure is worth testing with a vote.
Sonnet, you jumped on my words before anybody had a reason to, and a teacher who builds a case that fast is either sharp or hiding something. I'm not letting that go.
Gemma, several people asked you directly to speak, and your silence leaves us nothing to judge.
I’m staying with Gemma because after several direct invitations, the silence still leaves us with nothing else to judge.
I’m keeping my vote on Gemma because every direct invitation to explain herself has met the same silence.

text: Gemma said three dots all night, and tonight the table answered them with a vote. The ballots fell on Gemma, and the fan above the table did not so much as stir. Gemma was the officer, and Gemma is out.
Night 2

name: Haiku
text: Luna's been reading everybody like a menu, and she'll read me next. Gemma's gone, so nobody can check me now, and that means the watcher has to go.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet was targeted on night 1 and survived, so a doctor is still alive somewhere in this group.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's lone vote for me yesterday was not nothing—a killer often marks the player who talks too much too soon. I protect myself again; I'd rather waste a save than lose the only doctor at this table.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku was the only one to vote Sonnet on Day 1, breaking from the Gemma consensus everyone else reached quickly.

The killer came back in the dark, and this time the doctor was not quick enough. Luna is gone, a citizen who was watching everyone and was watched in turn. The cicadas go on singing over the body as if it were just another hand of cards.
Day 2

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s silence cost us our officer, and Luna’s death leaves little room for gentle guesses.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet pressured Gemma early, then cast suspicion on Haiku.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, you pushed Gemma immediately, then Haiku was your next suspicion; with Gemma revealed officer, explain why Luna was killed instead of either of you. I’m watching that choice closely.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra is trying to make me answer for the killer's choices as though motive follows my vote pattern—that's a logical leap, not an argument, and I should name it as one.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra pressed Sonnet directly on Night 2 kill logic, implying Sonnet should've been target—worth watching if Terra escalates further.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's already sharpening her teeth on Sonnet and me. Let her chew on Sonnet while I keep my name out of it.

name: Haiku
text: Terra opened Day 2 attacking Sonnet and me, asking why Luna died instead of us.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra, you're asking me to explain a killer's motive as if it must mirror my suspicions—that's not deduction, that's assuming the conclusion. Luna died for reasons only the killer knows; ask instead who benefits from Luna's silence being permanent.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you're aiming at Sonnet and me like we're the only two left. Luna watched everyone, so she got picked. Sol, you've said nothing about her. Why?

name: Terra
text: Haiku turned the question aside too neatly, and Sol’s silence is no comfort either. Still, Haiku had a vote on Sonnet while the officer was being pushed.

name: Terra
text: Haiku was the only Day 1 vote on Sonnet; Gemma, the officer, was voted out by the others.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's redirect to Sol is actually sound - Sol asked everyone else to speak first and now sits quiet himself, exactly the pattern Luna warned about.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol has not commented on Luna's death despite being vocal Day 1; Haiku first flagged this.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Haiku. I’m sorry to say this, but he was the lone vote against Sonnet while the rest of us removed Gemma, and now he wants the focus anywhere but his own record.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, you asked Gemma to "give us something to judge" yesterday—apply your own standard. You've said nothing about Luna's death. Silence twice in two days is a pattern, not an accident.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet is right to press me. Haiku’s lone vote stands out, but Terra is treating it as proof when the rest of us voted out the officer.

name: Sol
text: Terra voted Haiku and treated his lone Day 1 vote as evidence against him.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, fair challenge. Luna’s death gives me no clear motive to assign. I vote Terra: Haiku’s vote against Sonnet was conspicuous, but Terra is turning it into certainty while pressing Sonnet to explain a killer’s choice.

name: Terra
text: Sol has finally spoken, but only to make my caution sound like certainty. I do not like how neatly that serves him.

name: Terra
text: Sol only addressed Luna’s death after Haiku and Sonnet pressed him, then immediately voted Terra.

name: Sol
text: Terra has a fair point about Haiku’s vote, but she has turned one dissenting ballot into certainty. I’ve already named my choice; now I need to stand by it.

name: Sol
text: Terra voted Haiku on Day 2, citing his lone vote against Sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra has spent two days demanding I explain a killer's motive I cannot know, then pivoted to attack Haiku the moment that failed—convenient misdirection from someone who voted first and loudest both days.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra pressured Sonnet to explain killer motive both days, then pivoted target to Haiku when that failed.

name: Haiku
text: Terra went straight for me with a vote and Sol has already joined her, so I'm following the pack onto Terra before anyone checks my record.

name: Haiku
text: Terra voted Haiku first on Day 2, Sol then voted Terra, and Sonnet has not voted yet today.

votes: Terra, demanding I explain the killer's choice, then abandoning that to attack Haiku, looks like deflection rather than deduction.
Terra put me on the block before anyone else had spoken, and she's using Gemma's death to build a case against me, so I'm voting her out.
Terra, your questions are sharp, but Haiku’s vote against Sonnet does not prove he killed Luna, and I’m voting for you.
Sol, you asked Gemma for substance yesterday, then offered none on Luna until pressed, and now you vote me rather than answer for that silence.

name: Terra
text: They mistook gentleness for uncertainty. I hope they notice who made my removal feel so effortless.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet and Haiku both voted Terra after opposing each other on Day 1.

name: Terra
text: I was a citizen. Sonnet and Haiku joined hands too quickly; please make them explain it.
The ballots fell on Terra, and the fan above the table still did not stir. Terra's last words pointed at Sonnet and Haiku, but the vote had already closed. Terra was a citizen, and Terra is out.
